paragraphs.text: Git worktree isolation for DeepSeek Harness: create a worktree, register it as its own project, and
start the session inside it
# @guowenzhang/dsh-worktree
English | 中文
## Why this plugin
Our project spans multiple repositories and needs parallel development. Git worktrees provide isolat
ed workspaces so file changes from different tasks do not interfere with each other.
This plugin lets you tick `worktree` on the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) New Session screen to create an i
solated workspace and start a session inside it. It can also set up submodules and nested repositori
es alongside the parent checkout.
In the plugin list, display names and descriptions follow the Harness language setting in English or
Chinese (English is the default fallback); English names use the package name without its npm scope
, Chinese names describe the purpose, and installation still uses the unchanged real package name.
## Screenshots
Select a base branch and tick `worktree` to create a workspace and open the new session. Unsent text
, references, and attachments move with it without being submitted; a failed creation or navigation
preserves the original draft.
The settings page carries three cards: **Git accounts** on top to connect GitHub / GitLab / Gitee, s
can this machine's existing authorizations, and jump to the Git accounts page for projects; **Worktr
ee settings** in the middle for whether new sessions start in a worktree, child repositories, scan d
epth, and storage location; and **Automatic backup** at the bottom for the protection switches and t
he change-history page. Valid changes save automatically and take effect immediately; no Save or Res
et to default button is needed.
## Protection before a change
**On by default.** The first time the AI is about to change a file that already exists, that file's
current content is copied out of the workspace — so a bad edit or a deletion can still be recovered.
The **Automatic backup** card on the settings page has three switch rows: **Session file protection*
* (on by default), **Block delete commands** (on by default), and **Show the change history sidebar*
* (on by default). Changes take effect immediately, with no restart.
Copies live in `~/.agents/file-guard/<session hash>/` and **mirror the workspace layout**, so recove
ry is copying the file back: no tool and no index needed. Files outside the working directory (anoth
er folder, another drive) go under `external/` with their own path preserved. **The copy is byte-lev
el, so format does not matter**: `.docx`, `.pptx`, and `.xlsx` are treated exactly like `.txt`.
Two things trigger a copy:
- **Automatic**: only `write` and `edit` copy their target *before* the write, at about 1 ms per fil

e. Read-only tools such as `read` and `read_image` do not create backups.
- **Declared by the model*
*: before changing files whose targets no argument names, the AI is asked to call the `worktree_back
up` tool with those paths. It has no scope limit — paths outside the working directory and on other
drives are accepted. **The result names the copy's absolute path**, so restoring a file never requir
es searching for it.
**Destructive shell commands are refused once.** A `bash` / `pwsh` command that looks like it delete
s files (`rm`, `del`, `rd`, `Remove-Item`, and so on) is denied, and the model is told to declare it
s targets through `worktree_backup` before retrying — a deletion cannot be recovered after it runs.
Quoted spans do not count, so `echo "rm -rf /"` is not refused. The switch can be turned off in sett
d spans do not count, so `echo "rm -rf /"` is not refused. The switch can be turned off in settings.
Rules worth knowing:
- **One copy per file.** A later change in the same session does not replace it, because the version

worth keeping is the one from before the first change.
[该节后续省略]
## Change history in the sidebar
**On by default.** The right sidebar offers a **Change history** page — open it from the sidebar's o
wn Start page, and use the page-refresh shortcut inside it to read the list again. It lists the file
s **this session and its sub-sessions changed or deleted**, one flat row each and no directory tree,
with only the path and a **Restore** button, without state badges. Deleted paths are struck through
; a successful restore removes the strike. A row a sub-session took names that sub-session, so it ca
nnot be confused with this session's file of the same path.
- **Modified** means the file's content no longer matches its copy; **Deleted** means the file is go

ne. A copy whose file is still byte-identical is left out, because there is nothing to restore.
- **
Restore** writes that one copy back over its file, creating the directories again if the file had be

en deleted. The copy itself is kept, so the same row can put the file back after a later change.
- *
*Compare** — click a row's path to open a two-column view: the copy from before this session first c
hanged the file on the left, the current file on the right, aligned line by line. Changed lines are
tinted and sit opposite each other; a collapsed band stands for a run of unchanged lines. Each side
scrolls sideways on its own because the two may have different line lengths, while vertical scrollin

g moves both together, and the view opens on the first change.
- The comparison compares **the two f
iles on disk — no Git involved**, so it works the same whether or not Git is installed. Its left sid
e is the state before this session's first change, so it shows everything changed since then, includ

ing edits another session made to a shared working directory.
- A binary file (`.docx`, `.xlsx`, an
image), a side over 2 MiB, or a path that is no longer a regular file is reported with its sizes ins
tead of a line comparison; **Restore stays available**. A very large text file shows the beginning o

f the comparison and says it is truncated.
[该节后续省略]
## Git accounts and projects
The left sidebar gains a **Git accounts** page that puts this machine's Git identity in one place: s
ign in to GitHub, GitLab (including self-hosted addresses such as `gitlab.arcuchi.com`), and Gitee;
set the global `user.name` and `user.email` used for commits; and browse your own projects.
[该节后续省略]
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart DSH after installation. Git must be installed and available on the host's PATH.
